sections.skill: Identify common scams and their warning signs, and respond safely

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: A caller says he is from the "Social Security office," your number is suspended, and you must pay today with gift cards. Which warning sign appears?

choices.text: The caller uses a polite tone of voice
Demanding payment by gift card
The call comes during business hours
The caller knows that you have a phone

questions.intro: Scam warning signs: a caller pretends to be from a trusted group, there is a problem or a prize, pressure to act now, and a demand to pay in a specific way (gift cards, wire transfer, cryptocurrency, or payment app). Government agencies do not demand gift cards.
questions.feedback: Real agencies never ask for payment by gift card.

misconceptions.A: Politeness is not a warning sign

sources: FTC (Scams): Scammers pretend to be from trusted organizations, create urgency, and ask for payment by gift card, wire, cryptocurrency, or payment app. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/features/scam-alerts)

FTC (Fake check scams): Banks must make deposited funds available quickly, but a fake check can bounce days later and the depositor must repay the bank. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-spot-avoid-and-report-fake-check-scams)

New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs: New Jersey residents can file consumer complaints with the Division of Consumer Affairs, which enforces the New Jersey Consumer Fraud Act. (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/)

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa sells a bike online for $300. The buyer mails a check for $1,500 and asks her to send back $1,200. Rosa deposits the check, ships the bike, and sends $1,200 by payment app. A week later the check bounces, and the bank takes back the $1,500; the other $300 of it is still in her account at that time. Not counting any bank fees, what has Rosa lost?

choices.text: Nothing, since the bank cleared the check
Only the $300 bike price
$1,200 plus the bike
$1,500 but she keeps the bike

questions.intro: In a fake check scam, the scammer overpays with a fake check and asks for the difference back. Banks make deposits available quickly, but the check can bounce days later and the depositor must repay the bank.
questions.feedback: The bank reverses the $1,500: $300 comes from what is left of the deposit, and the $1,200 she sent is gone, along with the bike she shipped.

misconceptions.A: "Available" does not mean the check is good

sources: FTC (Scams): Scammers pretend to be from trusted organizations, create urgency, and ask for payment by gift card, wire, cryptocurrency, or payment app. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/features/scam-alerts)

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: A job posting pays $40 an hour to "reship packages" after you pay $99 for a starter kit. What is the best response?

choices.text: Pay the fee because good jobs require investment
Give your bank login so they can send pay
Reship the packages to earn trust first
Avoid it; it shows scam signs

questions.correct_answer: Avoid it; it shows scam signs
questions.feedback: Paying to get a job and reshipping packages are classic scam signs.

misconceptions.A: Real employers do not charge to hire

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: A pop-up says Rosa's computer has a virus and to call a number for "tech support." What should she do?

choices.text: Close the page and not call
Call and give the support agent remote access
Pay with a gift card for a quick fix
Share her passwords so they can test them

questions.correct_answer: Close the page and not call
questions.feedback: Real tech companies do not use pop-ups with phone numbers; close it and run trusted security software.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa was scammed. Where should she report it?

choices.text: Only to the scammer, to ask for a refund
ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Nowhere, since reporting does nothing
A website that promises to recover money for a fee

questions.intro: Report fraud to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov, to your bank or payment app right away, and to state agencies such as the New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs.
questions.feedback: The FTC collects scam reports; contact your bank quickly too.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: An online friend Rosa has never met asks her to receive money and forward it. What is she being asked to do?

choices.text: Act as a money mule
Join a legitimate savings club
Open a normal business account
Help a charity process donations

questions.intro: Money mules move stolen money for criminals, often recruited online. It can lead to frozen accounts and criminal charges.
questions.feedback: Forwarding money for strangers can make you a money mule.
